affected_system: drinking-water distribution, sewer collection, pumping, and treatment assets
alternatives: rank verified high-consequence candidates for water and wastewater renewal portfolio
select a risk-, equity-, and lifecycle-balanced portfolio for water and wastewater renewal portfolio
pair condition, consequence, compliance, equity, and lifecycle optimization with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Assets, inspections, breaks, overflows, pressure, flow, quality, work, and complaints remain distinct.
Hydraulic, process, condition, and consequence models receive utility engineering review.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
baseline: fund only already-committed work for water and wastewater renewal portfolio.

constraints.description: The water and wastewater infrastructure prioritize must respect declared capital, operating, maintenance, and delivery budgets.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
decision_owner: water and wastewater utility asset director
decision_question: Which pipes, pumps, plants, storage, sensors, and process upgrades should enter the capital portfolio?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The water and wastewater infrastructure prioritize must respect declared capital, operating, maintenance, and delivery budgets.
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for water and wastewater renewal portfolio passes documented checks for cost, benefit, service life, dependencies, deliverability, and maintenance burden.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: condition, consequence, compliance, equity, and lifecycle optimization
independence_key.primary_outcome: expected risk-adjusted service interruption and compliance burden

intended_claim: A versioned prioritize design for comparing declared alternatives affecting water and wastewater renewal portfolio, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: expected risk-adjusted service interruption and compliance burden
distributional gap in expected risk-adjusted service interruption and compliance burden
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not report modeled risk reduction as completed renewal, compliance, or avoided incidents.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for water and wastewater renewal portfolio passes documented checks for cost, benefit, service life, dependencies, deliverability, and maintenance burden.

title: Prioritize water and wastewater renewal
transportability_risks: Network age, materials, soils, climate, regulation, treatment, hydraulics, and costs differ.
Published incidents and complaints can omit failures or lack asset-level linkage.
